citeAs: Langlais, P.-C., Rosas Hinostroza, C., Nee, M., Amett, C., Chizhov, P., Jones, E. K., Girard, I., Mach, D., Stasenko, A., & Yamshchikov, I. P. (2025). Common Corpus: The Largest Collection of Ethical Data for LLM Pre-Training. arXiv preprint arXiv:2506.01732.
creator: Pierre-Carl Langlais, Carlos Rosas Hinostroza, Mattia Nee, Catherine Amett, Pavel Chizhov, Eliot Krzystof Jones, Irène Girard, David Mach, Anastasia Stasenko, Ivan P. Yamshchikov (PleIAs)
description: Common Corpus is the largest open dataset for language model pre-training, containing about two trillion tokens of data that are either uncopyrighted or under permissible licenses.
inLanguage: en, fr, de, es, la, it, pl, el, pt, ru
license: Public Domain, CC-By, MIT, CC-By-SA, Apache-2.0, BSD-3-Clause, Open license, BSD-2-Clause, CC-BY-4.0, CC0-1.0
name: Common Corpus
rai:dataBiases: The dataset mitigates potential biases and harms by identifying documents containing harmful language (along five dimensions: race and origin-based bias, gender and sexuality-based bias, religious bias, ability bias, and violence and abuse) and either removing them or synthetically rewriting the document without the harmful language.
rai:dataCollection: Common Corpus is composed of six collections: Open Government, Open Culture, Open Science, Open Web, Open Code, and Open Semantic, aggregated from various open sources, public domain archives, and permissible web data.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw sources include mediawiki syntax for Wikipedia, raw XML output (METS/ALTO) for cultural heritage datasets, and uncorrected OCR-ed texts from digitized books and newspapers.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: The documents come from a wide time range, spanning from the 17th century (e.g., Caselaw Access Project spans 1658 to 2020) up to 2024.
rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Document analysis, Software Collection
rai:dataLimitations: Common Corpus is far from collecting the whole range of available open data, the coverage for low-resource languages is still shallow, and it does not contain data for instruction-tuning or specialized tasks.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Documents containing harmful language are either removed or synthetically rewritten without the harmful language. OCR errors are corrected using the OCRonos model, which can act as a synthetic rewriting tool on highly deteriorated content.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Text segmentation is performed using Segmentext. OCR quality is evaluated using OCRoscope and OCRerrcr, and corrected using OCRonos. Personally Identifiable Information (PII) is identified using Microsoft's Presidio and replaced with fictitious but realistic values.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Common Corpus will remain an evolving resource reflecting the need for a continuous open infrastructure rather than a fixed dataset, with HuggingFace ensuring a proper archiving of past versions for reproducibility.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Common Corpus aims to support the pre-training of fully open and auditable LLMs by making it legal to release the source even without the provision of fair use, contributing to the AI Commons and open science research.
rai:dataUseCases: Pre-training Large Language Models, developing vision-language models for document segmentation, training models for creative writing, and creating historical language models.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Segmentext (text segmentation), OCRoscope and OCRerrcr (OCR error detection), OCRonos (OCR correction), Microsoft Presidio (PII detection), and Celadon (toxicity classifier).
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Personally Identifiable Information (PII) such as phone numbers, email addresses, and IP addresses are identified and replaced with fictitious but realistic values.
